newsitem.title: UK: Cola-makers marketing aggressively to win business.
newsitem.headline: Cola-makers marketing aggressively to win business.

text.p: Cola manufacturers are turning to increasingly aggressive marketing tactics in their battle for part of the world's $167 billion cola market, Euromonitor research group said on Monday.
"Millions of dollars are spent each year on advertising and packaging by PepsiCo and Coca-Cola," it said in a report called "Global Soft Drinks."
Euromonitor said Coca-Cola was placing great emphasis on its "contour" bottle, while PepsiCo was rolling out worldwide the blue packaging it launched last year.
PepsiCo's ad campaign for this year includes scenes shot on the Russian Mir space station at a cost of about $1.5 million, said Euromonitor.
According to the report, global retail sales of soft drinks grew by 28 percent between 1992 and 1996 to $167 billion.
North America is the world's largest market accounting for nearly 49 percent of value sales worldwide, followed by western Europe with 18.4 percent of sales.
Fizzy drinks represent the largest sector of the market with sales of more than 90 billion in 1996.

However, Euromonitor said that as consumers opt to lead healthier lifestyles in many developed markets, consumption of alcohol and sugary carbonated drinks is generally being reduced in favour of bottled water and fruit juices.

Both Coca-Cola and PepsiCo have entered these markets and in order to gain access to the tea and coffee-based drinks sector, have formed joint ventures or alliances rather than develop their own brands, said the report.
PepsiCo has teamed up with Unilever, which owns the Lipton tea brand, and Coca-Cola has joined forces with Nestle, which is involved in the fruit juice and bottled water markets.
According to Euromonitor, by the year 2001 the soft drinks market will have continued to rise to achieve retail sales of more than $207 billion.
Carbonated drinks will still be the largest sector of the market with sales expected to exceed $112 billion.
